properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/05/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Jefferson Township, Fayette county. OGA3216(B) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - PLAN - Failure to follow E&S control plan during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/05/2026
Violation Code: OGA3216(B) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - PLAN - Failure to follow E&S control plan during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities.
Violation ID: 8267020
Permit API: 051-22256
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Jefferson Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/05/2026
Comments: On March 5, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4151444.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. Stage of plugging operations was not confirmed during this inspection.RCE is not installed as depicted on the E and S plan. Surface/vegetation disturbance beyond the width of the access road remains near the entrance as observed in IR 4151444. Plastic matting on access road remains in the same two areas (Photos 7-10).CFS is observed along the access road only on either side of the road at the pre-existing culvert (Photos 11-16). Both sections of CFS are not installed properly as stakes are missing and/or are separated by 10 or more feet between stakes. The CFS on the culvert's outlet side is currently overtopping and causing an erosion channel to begin to form downslope of the CFS. Sediment is not observed to be discharging into the Waters of the Commonwealth at this time.Production tank is observed contained within an adequately vegetated earthen berm. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at the production tank at this time. Pooling of stormwater is observed along the access road closer to the site (Photos 22-23). This water is observed to be exiting the access road and causing an erosion channel to begin to form downslope. No CFS is observed at this area.CFS is observed to be present along the downslope side of the well site as depicted in the E and S plan, however it is not properly installed as stakes are missing and/or are separated by 10 or more feet between stakes (Photos 24-25). Water is currently pooling along the CFS at an area where the stakes have been removed from the surface.The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator maintain all BMPs on-site and install additional controls where necessary, as per the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator seed and mulch or otherwise temporarily stabilize the affected areas of erosion.Violations are continued for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan and for improperly installed CFS.New violations are being issued for erosion and sedimentation and additional sections of improperly installed CFS.

Violation ID: 980668
Permit API: 129-27065
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: North Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/04/2023
Comments: On January 4, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Bozich 2 well site in North Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself and DEP OGI Patrick Hiles. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3453961, during which remediation efforts were made by the operator in response to IR 3446144, where impacted soil was discovered by the Department.The following was observed:The well site excavation has been backfilled since IR 3453961 (see photos 2 and 5). The site appeared to be stabile with no concerns related to accelerated erosion or sedimentation, and was mulched and seeded. The excavation stockpile remains placed atop a sheet of black plastic (see photo 1). However, it was uncovered unlike the operator and contractor reported. The well head was equipped with a well tag (see photo 3). The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of leaks or discharge (see photo 4). Soil conductivity readings were taken around the excavation stockpile to ensure that contamination has not leached into the ground. Elevated conductivity was found immediately downslope of the stockpile, on its west side (see photos 6, 7, and 9). Additional readings were taken approximately 4 feet further downslope from this point, and around the rest of the stockpile (see photos 8, 10, 11, and 12). No additional elevated readings were gathered. Soil conductivity readings were also taken in the backfilled area around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to the surrounding soil (see photos 13, 14, and 15). A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 170 Microsiemens (see photo 16). Based on observations from this inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been excavated from the area of release. However, the contaminants contained within the excavation stockpile appear to be washing downslope into the surrounding soil, and is therefore not being properly stored and/or contained. Because this contamination appears to be localized close to the stockpile, the Department recommends immediate remediation and proper storage to prevent the contamination from spreading. Also, the Department once again requests an approximate quantity released from the brine tank, and the waste manifest when available.

Elevated conductivity was found immediately downslope of the stockpile, on its west side (see photos 6, 7, and 9). Additional readings were taken approximately 4 feet further downslope from this point, and around the rest of the stockpile (see photos 8, 10, 11, and 12). No additional elevated readings were gathered. Soil conductivity readings were also taken in the backfilled area around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to the surrounding soil (see photos 13, 14, and 15). A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 170 Microsiemens (see photo 16). Based on observations from this inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been excavated from the area of release. However, the contaminants contained within the excavation stockpile appear to be washing downslope into the surrounding soil, and is therefore not being properly stored and/or contained. Because this contamination appears to be localized close to the stockpile, the Department recommends immediate remediation and proper storage to prevent the contamination from spreading. Also, the Department once again requests an approximate quantity released from the brine tank, and the waste manifest when available.

Comments: On 11/3/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. It was 68 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration areas. They are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.While on site, I witnessed an 8" x 24" water puddle below a rock stabilized area on the fill slope where high conductance water had been found in previous inspections. The water puddle field tested at 2.89 mS conductance. I also witnessed a 1' x 5' water puddle below this in the infiltration area 1 that field tested at 2.46 mS conductance. There was a 10' x 25' water puddle on the pad surface next to the perimeter berm above these two locations that field tested at 1.713 mS conductance. I collected water samples from these three areas. Other water puddles on the pad surface tested at 1.6 mS and 1.7 mS conductanceThere were ten wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. Six of the ten GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks and two gas busters on location located in secondary containment.The DEP recommends the following:1. Assess the various areas with elevated conductance and repair/report as necessary. 2. Provide immediate protection as necessary to prevent pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. After the inspection, I discussed the elevated conductance with Chesapeake's Eric Hottenstein. He agreed to look into the issue and to confer with Chesapeake personnel on possible additional measures to perform at the site.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3406647 for high conductance fluid escaping from damaged containment during well stimulation activities with unknown volume impacting the pad surface. I left the site at 1510

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/6/2023 at 1430 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Blackhill. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #371191 is tied to this release within CTS. On 4/6/2023 at ~1300 hours an initial estimate of 4 barrels of produced water was discovered by Blackhill Energy to have been released from the produced water offload area at the Jackson pad. Prior to my arrival, the estimate was increased to a potential 7 barrels of produced water. The release occurred when the offload valve for the produced water tanks was not closed all the way after offloading. The valve is held in a yellow bin and the produced water was discovered to be leaking from the bin shown in photo #2. As it leaked from the bin, part of the release was contained to secondary containment and part of the release was spilled to the pad surface. During my inspection, fluids located on the pad surface in the known impacted area from the release were field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photos #1 and 2). After inspecting the rock-lined conveyance channel located just west of the release area (photo #4) it was discovered that elevated conductivity fluids were located in the channel. I field measured fluids in the rock-lined conveyance channel along the entirety of the southern edge of the pad. All fluids in the rock-lined channel up to the stormwater control basin were field measured at >19.99mS/cm. Fluid flowing in the rock-lined channel was observed entering the stormwater control basin. I collected a sample (0983-377) for standard analysis code 942 from the fluid located in the rock-lined conveyance channel just before entering the stormwater control basin (photo #11). This fluid was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photo #10). Two sumps were constructed along the rock-lined channel to begin collecting any fluids flowing in the channel. The DEP requested that the now impacted stormwater contained in the stormwater basin be collected as a regulated substance due to the release impacting it. As I departed a crew were working on excavating the impacted pad material near the point of release and recovering the fluids that were on the surface of the pad. Temporary storage containers were scheduled to be brought in to be staged onsite for storage of the stormwater control basin's water. Plans to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment to begin excavating beneath it were also being made. The drain pipe of the stormwater basin was believed to be clogged but was also closed as a precaution. I departed the site at 1600 hours. Based on the reported release of produced water outside of containment and the discovery of the release entering conveyance channels and reaching the stormwater controls, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23733: 25 Pa. Prior to my arrival, the estimate was increased to a potential 7 barrels of produced water. The release occurred when the offload valve for the produced water tanks was not closed all the way after offloading. The valve is held in a yellow bin and the produced water was discovered to be leaking from the bin shown in photo #2. As it leaked from the bin, part of the release was contained to secondary containment and part of the release was spilled to the pad surface. During my inspection, fluids located on the pad surface in the known impacted area from the release were field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photos #1 and 2). After inspecting the rock-lined conveyance channel located just west of the release area (photo #4) it was discovered that elevated conductivity fluids were located in the channel. Temporary storage containers were scheduled to be brought in to be staged onsite for storage of the stormwater control basin's water. Plans to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment to begin excavating beneath it were also being made. The drain pipe of the stormwater basin was believed to be clogged but was also closed as a precaution. I departed the site at 1600 hours. Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted and INCIDENT inspection of the SWEPI LP - Kennedy 137 well pad located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 4/15/2019 @1000 hours the weather was 43 degrees, rain, winds W 18mph. Approximately 0.6 inches of precipitation was received over the past 24 hours. On 4/14/2019 @1700 hours, Shell representatives called in a spill of a reported 90 BBLs of production fluid to the pad surface of the Kennedy 137. A truck driver had discovered a hose connected to one of the Highland production tanks that was discharging production fluid to the pad surface. The driver assumed the Highland tank was at maximum capacity when it discharged it's contents. Mr. Bernethy, SWEPI Environmental Coordinator, contacted the WQS this morning to state the driver was mistaken. The Highland tank was not at capacity and the revised amount of the spill is 3-4 BBLs. As of yesterday evening, a vac truck had removed standing fluid from the pad surface,and a sump was constructed below the discharge valve from the Highland tank to remove accumulated fluid. Mr. Bernethy stated the sump will be regularly monitored and fluid removed as needed. As of today's inspection, no personnel were observed onsite. The impacted area below the Highland tank was observed flagged with cones and spray paint. The constructed sump was observed, and the fluid being held had a field measured conductivity of 1.00 mS/cm. All other puddles screened on the pad surface had a field measured conductivity of <1.0mS/cm. The fluid in the E&S channel below the fill slope was screened and found to be <1.0mS/cm. The E&S trap below the fill slope was also screened and found to be <1.0mS/cm. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time do to the reported release of 3-4 barrels of production fluid to the pad surface: CSL402b Potential Pollution SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.57 control, storage and disposal of production fluids. We departed the site @ 1100 hours.

Report Details

Violation Date: 2/10/2026
Violation Code: 78A55(I)5I_ - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Planning – Operator’s emergency response plan failed to incorporate National Incident Management System planning standards, including the use of the Incident Command System, Incident Action Planning and Common Communications Plans.
Violation ID: 8264364
Permit API: 059-25724
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/10/2026
Comments: On 02/10/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 2/09/2026 from Greylock (CTS #395045). I was accompanied by Madison Raviart (PA DEP Water Quality Specialist) and Greylock representative Trevor Wood. Per Greylock, the spill was reported to the Department's emergency hotline on 02/09/2026. It was reported that 1-3 bbls of brine water released onto the pad on 02/09/2026. The spill was identified at 4:00 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 7:13 PM. Gravel and snow was impacted on the pad and the spill was contained to the pad and snow was hand shoveled into tanks containment. No waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. There was no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite at the site entrance (Photo 1). I recommend these be added to site near the site entrance. The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).Cinders were placed on road coming up to the pad on 02/10/2026 (Photos 3-5). Snow around the containment for the tanks was hand shoveled and put into the containment (Photo 6). The spill originated from a separator on the pad. High pressure caused brine water to come out of the separator and spray onto the pad and tank. 1-3 barrels (bbls) were released (Photos 7-10). Conductivity readings taken in the middle of the impacted area ranged from 2.09 mS/cm-4.55mS/cm (Photos 11,12). Conductivity reading taken in gravel on the opposite side of the entrance in front of separators was 252 S/cm (Photo 13). Conductivity readings taken along tank containment ranged from 709 S/cm-8.61 mS/cm (Photos 14-18).The area was still in the process of remediation and Greylock was waiting on additional equipment to begin remediation. The spill appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. I recommend following Act 2 guidelines.Due to the release of brine water and no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite, violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78A55(I)5I, and 78a66(b)2.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/14/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8158549
Permit API: 033-25118
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Bell Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/14/2023
Comments: The Department received a complaint on 9/11/23 regarding a potential brine leak on the ground at conventional well 033-25118. I conducted a site inspection on 9/14/23. I observed a bare spot of soil inundated with deer hoof prints near the valve on the brine tank. An area of dead and/or stressed vegetation was also observed. In addition, some standing puddles were observed near the brine tank and in a ditch approximately 20' away from the brine tank. I screened the puddles using an Oakton meter for conductivity. Readings ranged from 16.93 mS/cm to 4.23 mS/cm. A grab sample was collected (3442-696) from one of the puddles near the brine tank and was sent to the Departments lab in Harrisburg to be tested for SAC 942 plus aluminum, bromide, and lithium. Based off screenings and dead vegetation the impacted area is at 20' x20'. After leaving the site I contacted Heather Empfield and Mark McCracken of Diversified and reported my findings. The Department recommends that operator investigates the brine release and based off the amount of brine released, the operator addresses the remediation in accordance with small spill policy 800-5000-001 or Act 2.Violations have been citied.

Violation ID: 8223943
Permit API: 003-22235
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/05/2025
Comments: On March 5, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection at the Oliver East well pad in Forward Township, Allegheny County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3913651. IR 3913651 was conducted in response to the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure which reportedly released 5-10 gallons of produced water to the surface of the well pad. Notice of Termination request was approved by the Department for this site on November 10, 2022.The following was observed:The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 21). The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 22). The well pad appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 1). Sediment from the access road appears to threaten a stormwater drain along Williamsport Road (see photo 23). Although no sediment was observed inside this stormwater drain at the time of inspection, a layer of sediment was observed on debris that had accumulated on top of the storm drain grate.The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 3). Well 4H is equipped with a well tag with no evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be equipped for production (see photos 5 and 6). There are fourteen additional well heads onsite that also appear to be in production (see photo 4). An additional storage tank placed within secondary containment was observed onsite (see photo 7). This secondary containment appears to be holding a significant amount of rainwater at the time of inspection. Old GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 9). However, their associated wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. New GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 8).A reported absorbent material has been applied to the majority of the area impacted by the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure (see photos 10-12). The conductivity of the soil underneath this reported absorbent material remains significantly higher than the surrounding soil (see photos 13-20). The soil conductivity meter utilized for this inspection was calibrated immediately prior to conducting this inspection. Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that not all impacted material has been removed and therefore remediation appears to be incomplete. Comments: On March 5, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection at the Oliver East well pad in Forward Township, Allegheny County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3913651. IR 3913651 was conducted in response to the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure which reportedly released 5-10 gallons of produced water to the surface of the well pad. Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a compliance evaluation inspection of Blackhill Energy's Kline A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 12/26/2023 at 0950 hours. The weather was 41 degrees with cloudy skies and light rain. An Act 9 sign remains in place at the site entrance. Environmental Trainees Erica Lutz and Evan Buck accompanied me during the inspection.On 11/30/2023 elevated conductivity fluids were observed outside of secondary containment summarized in inspection report #3655668. Sample 0983-405 was collected for standard analysis code (SAC) 942 on 11/30/2023. Those sample results are attached as a file and as photos (photos #6 and 7). During today's inspection, fluid outside of secondary containment was field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) ranging from 275 to 1200us/cm. The pad area impacted from the elevated conductivity fluids that was observed on 11/30/2023 was observed to be cleaned up to visible. Blackhill Energy provided a 15-day notice of violation (NOV) response to the violation cited on 11/30/2023 to the DEP on 12/13/2023. The NOV response is attached to this inspection report as a file and will be uploaded to eFACTS.Secondary containment structures onsite appear to be in working condition and no leaks or tears were observed during today's inspection. Pooled water held within the secondary containments that was field measured for EC ranged from 220 to 1530us/cm. Numerous temporary storage containers and evaporators are held within secondary containment onsite. Based on the analytical results from sample # 0983-405 and Blackhill Energy's timely remediation of the area of concern noted on 11/30/2023, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #015-23867:SWMA 30125 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)The CSL402(b) violation cited against API #015-23867 on 11/30/2023 is now considered closed. We departed the site at 1050 hours.

OGA3216(C) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - PITS, DRILLING SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT - Failure to fill all pits used to contain produced fluids or industrial wastes and remove unnecessary drilling supplies/equipment not needed for production within 9 months from completion of drilling of well.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: OGA3216(C) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - PITS, DRILLING SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT - Failure to fill all pits used to contain produced fluids or industrial wastes and remove unnecessary drilling supplies/equipment not needed for production within 9 months from completion of drilling of well.
Violation ID: 8250022
Permit API: 125-29133
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Blaine Township
Inspection Type: Site Restoration
Inspection Date: 9/23/2025
Comments: On September 23, 2025, the DEP conducted an inspection at the Schwotzer Arthur well site. This inspection was conducted in response to a Post-Drilling Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) that was submitted by the operator on August 6, 2025 for well 6H (125-29133). A notarized Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration was submitted with the WSRR, as sound walls currently remain onsite. Total Depth was obtained on November 17, 2024 according to the Well Record, therefore site restoration is to be complete by August 17, 2025.An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit (ESP07632300100E) was issued by the DEP for this site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029.The following was observed:Accumulated fine sediment from the access road was observed in the rock-lined channel along Rural Valley Road (photo 3). This sedimentation has not reached the storm culvert where it empties (photo 4). No accelerated erosion rills were observed on the access road and well pad at the time of inspection (photos 2, 9, and 21). Exposed soil was observed in several areas onsite which appear to require additional temporary stabilization (photos 6 and 19). The soil crack that was present on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad appears to be repaired. Riprap has been added to this location to improve drainage (photo 12). No toe bulge was observed below at the time of inspection. Repair work has been conducted on the slough that occurred on the well pad cutslope, with no loose sediment observed in the vegetated channel below (photos 14-18). What appears to be surface cracking was observed at the top of well pad cut slope (photo 20). This appears to be due to recent excessive dryness onsite. No toe bulge was observed belowThe Act 9 sign is fully visible at the entrance of the access road, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 22). The GPU units onsite are equipped with interconnected drip pans (photo 23). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the DEP for use on 6/21/2022. Well 6H is equipped with a well tag and appears to be in production (photo 24). No evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it was observed. There are six additional well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Well permits, Individual E and S permit approval letter, E and S permit drawings, and E and S inspection log are onsite (photo 25). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the information required by 78a.55.Based on observations from this inspection, the WSRR is denied. Because the well site is not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth, violations are being issued for failure to restore 9 months post-drilling.While the DEP was onsite, Jessica Ullom from Range Resources arrived onsite. The DEP spoke with Ullom to inform them of the forthcoming recommendations in this inspection report.The DEP recommends that the access road is maintained in a manner that prevents fine sediment from accumulating further in stormwater discharge areas, including by conducting maintenance in accordance with the access road cross section shown on page C134 of site permit plans. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further assessment and evaluation in a future follow up inspection.The DEP also recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the site and implement temporary stabilization where exposed soil is found. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further assessment and evaluation in a future follow up inspection. Finally, the DEP recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the soil cracking at the top of the well pad cutslope to determine whether it threatens site stability or is due to recent dry conditions, and that the operator notify the DEP of findings.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: HILCORP ENERGY CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/14/2024
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8208635
Permit API: 073-20398
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lawrence
Municipality: Pulaski Township
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 11/14/2024
Comments: Arrived on location in the morning on 11/14/2024 with cold, overcast, rainy weather conditions, and 36 degrees. Met with Operator representatives, Brian Reynolds and Chris McCoy, and PADEP representatives OGIS Rick Willey, OGI Thomas Antonishak, and OGI Kyle Thomas to obtain a status of operation activities. Currently, reentered well with 2 7/8" working string drill pipe (DP); tagged hard at ~8 feet; present depth is 10 feet as circulating gravel out of hole begins (photo #1). Operator representative, Brian Reynolds stated that the BOPs and subfloor components/sections were all tested to 2,500 psi and passed. Late last night, 11/13/2024 the well was secured and shut in overnight. He also stated the well had 70 psi pressure this morning when they opened well for reentry. On site meeting with Operator representative, Chris McCoy and PADEP representatives OGIS Rick Willey, OGI Thomas Antonishak, and OGI Kyle Thomas to discuss the Operators current plans for identifying where the leaking gas is occurring and plans for replugging to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore. Discussions around well being originally plugged not to regulations and how to become compliant occurred. To be in compliance, the Operator (Hilcorp) will need to drill out cement plugs in the 9 5/8" and 5 1/2" down to the cement at 4,696' directly above the CIBP. Plug #2 set as Class A cement from depths 4,696' to 5,100'. This cement plug is atop Plug #1 as mechanical CIBP set at depth of 5,100'. Once atop this cement Plug #2 with working string, the Operator will have to pressure up and test the integrity of this plug. Based on the results of integrity testing will determine if replugging can continue out of the hole with an Alternate Method, approved by the Department or if additional discussions and game-planning is needed. Operator representative Chris McCoy will be drafting a plan/procedure to capture the discussion and operation activities going forward to test the integrity of the deepest set plug(s). Currently, continuing to go in hole with working string, circulating and cleaning out wellbore with a pump rate of 5 bbls/minute with a 1,200 psi output. Depart location.

Report Details

Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 948222
Permit API: 035-21325
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2022
Comments: On March 16, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline and Brooke Millisock conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The DEP observed and sampled five seeps and four stream sites that were found off the west side of the well pad in "Deep Hollow" along an UNT to Rattlesnake Run. STL Resources revealed that the seeps were occurring and being monitored for specific conductivity and chlorides on March 1, 2022 during a meeting with the DEP. The data that STL Resources provided showed levels of elevated conductivity in seeps 1, 1A, and 4. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling site for pH and conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 had a pH of 8.61 and conductivity of 29.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 had pH of 7.97 and a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 had pH of 7.18 and a conductivity of 22.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 had a pH of 6.84 and a conductivity of 22.2. Seep 1 had a pH of 5.14 and a conductivity of 308 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a pH of 5.04 and a conductivity of 345 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a pH of 6.62 and a conductivity of 43.2 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a pH of 6.3 and a conductivity of 42.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a pH of 6.25 and a conductivity of 191.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had pH of 8.01 and a conductivity of 28.2 uS/cm. Water quality samples 0651-104, 106, 108, and 111 were collected at the four stream sampling sites and submitted for SAC code 942 plus Aluminum, Lithium, and Bromide. Water quality samples 0651-105, 107, 109, and 110 were collected at seeps 1,1A, 4, and 5. Water quality sample 0651-112 was collected in a channel downgradient of Seeps 2 and 3 due to not enough water available to sample in these seeps. An additional seep was observed up the logging road of Seep 3, this seep had pH of 6.67 and conductivity of 22.5. The previously mentioned seep did not appear to be monitored by STL Resources. The southwest infiltration berm excavation area remains uncovered and the stormwater level in the area as begun to recede eliminating the overflowing of the area. The water level in the southwest stormwater vault was about a foot deep and was unable to be screened for conductivity. The water level in the northwest stormwater vault was about 18 inches and could not be screened for conductivity. The seeps that were observed near the northwest stormwater vault on March 3, 2022 were not flowing at the time of inspection. A new area of excavation was observed where the water from these seeps was pooling. This area has been covered with a tarp. There was water pooled on top of the tarp and next to the tarp. The conductivity of this water was 3,400 uS/cm. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources said they will continue to vacuum the pooling water as necessary. The pooled water in this area could be seen overflowing into an adjacent depression that was covered with a tarp. The DEP recommends exploring this area and removing any contaminated water and soil. STL Resources has removed the contaminated soil stockpile that was being staged on the well pad. Well Pad remediation from the spill that occurred on January 8, 2022 has not occurred. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 had pH of 7.97 and a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 had pH of 7.18 and a conductivity of 22.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 had a pH of 6.84 and a conductivity of 22.2. Seep 1 had a pH of 5.14 and a conductivity of 308 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a pH of 5.04 and a conductivity of 345 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a pH of 6.62 and a conductivity of 43.2 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a pH of 6.3 and a conductivity of 42.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a pH of 6.25 and a conductivity of 191.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had pH of 8.01 and a conductivity of 28.2 uS/cm. Water quality samples 0651-104, 106, 108, and 111 were collected at the four stream sampling sites and submitted for SAC code 942 plus Aluminum, Lithium, and Bromide. Water quality samples 0651-105, 107, 109, and 110 were collected at seeps 1,1A, 4, and 5. Water quality sample 0651-112 was collected in a channel downgradient of Seeps 2 and 3 due to not enough water available to sample in these seeps. An additional seep was observed up the logging road of Seep 3, this seep had pH of 6.67 and conductivity of 22.5. The previously mentioned seep did not appear to be monitored by STL Resources. The southwest infiltration berm excavation area remains uncovered and the stormwater level in the area as begun to recede eliminating the overflowing of the area. The water level in the southwest stormwater vault was about a foot deep and was unable to be screened for conductivity. The water level in the northwest stormwater vault was about 18 inches and could not be screened for conductivity. The seeps that were observed near the northwest stormwater vault on March 3, 2022 were not flowing at the time of inspection. A new area of excavation was observed where the water from these seeps was pooling. This area has been covered with a tarp. There was water pooled on top of the tarp and next to the tarp. The conductivity of this water was 3,400 uS/cm. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources said they will continue to vacuum the pooling water as necessary. The pooled water in this area could be seen overflowing into an adjacent depression that was covered with a tarp. The DEP recommends exploring this area and removing any contaminated water and soil. STL Resources has removed the contaminated soil stockpile that was being staged on the well pad. Well Pad remediation from the spill that occurred on January 8, 2022 has not occurred. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: On July 10, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Complete Inspection of Monona's Stickle 1H well site located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County. Accompanying on today's inspection is Tyler Metzger (WQS DEP).At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance, the Department recommends the Operator replace the Act 9 Sign with one that satisfies 78a55(i)4ii. In the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan, however it had a different Operator's name posted on it, the Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site perimeters appeared to be exhibiting at last 70% uniform and adequate vegetative cover.At the time of this inspection, the Stickle 1H well site appeared to have 2 wells on it, the 1H (permit number 129-28411) had a well tag fixed to the wellhead with the well's name and permit number on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead.A plethora of production equipment that did not appear to equipped for production was observed in several locations of the well site, the Department recommends all equipment not currently in use be removed from the well site.2 production tanks were observed to be within a secondary containment that had a minimal amount of fluid pooled in it as well as an unlabeled barrel. The production tanks appeared to be heavily corroded with several holes observed at the top of the tank located on the right-hand side. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tanks to ensure further corrosion and a release of production fluids does not occur. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed several areas of the graveled well pad to have an oily substance on it, specifically in areas relating to the reported re-plugging of the 129-28648 well. Violations were issued against the 129-28648 well for a release(s) of an oily substance.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the Act 9 Sign not in compliance, the outdated ERP and for the corrosion holes in the production tank.
